chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is not compulsory for the creation to recognize Allah until He introduces Himself to them. It is compulsory for Allah that He introduces Himself to the creation. It is compulsory for the creation to accept Allah when He introduces Himself to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of Allah towards His creation regarding self-revelation and recognition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the divine pedagogy of *ma'rifah* (gnosis), establishing that God’s self-revelation precedes human obligation, thereby affirming His justice in requiring only what He has first made known. It underscores the reciprocal covenant where divine guidance necessitates human acceptance, a core tenet in Shia theological discourse on the balance between divine grace and human responsibility.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Abu Shu`ayb al-Mahamili, on the authority of Durust ibn Abu Mansur, on the authority of Burayd ibn Mua`wiyah al-`Ijli that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

It is not compulsory for the creation to recognize Allah until He introduces Himself to them. It is compulsory for Allah that He introduces Himself to the creation. It is compulsory for the creation to accept Allah when He introduces Himself to them.
